title: City-paid firms and the State contractor-licence file
question: Does the State’s licence file show a problem with a firm the City pays, or tie it to a firm that has one?
finding: 516 City-paid firms match a State contractor licence by name; 13 of those licences are shown as suspended, 10 of them for firms paid $65.1 million since July 2024; 1 City-paid firm shares a State-numbered licensed person with a firm the City has barred, and 10 with a suspended licence.
how: City vendors paid $100,000 or more since fiscal 2019 are matched to the State licence master by exact business name. The State gives every person on a licence a number; where one number sits on two licences, the same person stands behind both. Persons are not named.
limits: Name matching can pick the wrong company, and large firms hold several licences. Most suspensions here are paperwork (a bond or insurance certificate not renewed) and many of these firms are paid for goods, power or software that need no contractor licence. The State file leaves out revoked and cancelled licences entirely, so the worst cases cannot appear. A licensed person moving from one firm to another is ordinary.
